evidence.effect: Market intraday momentum ROD -> LH (rest-of-day return predicts last half hour), lean hogs alone
evidence.rule: r_LH on r_ROD, r_ROD = P(C-30)/P(prior close)-1, C = 13:05 CT (paper's LH hours 08:30-13:05); long if r_ROD>0, short if <0, exit at C
evidence.conversion: slope 0.03 (x100) = 0.0003: a 1% r_ROD predicts 0.0003% = 0.03 bp = 0.01 tick; HE tick 0.025 c/lb x 40,000 lb = $10; at the 80 c/lb price level the source itself uses (He 2022, p.16: 'a lean hog contract with a unit price of 80 cents/pound'), 1 tick = 0.025/80 = 3.125 bp
evidence.decay_evidence: Null in full sample: t 0.06, adjusted R2 -0.01%, R2_OOS -0.06% (no in-sample or OOS predictability)
evidence.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021), Hedging demand and market intraday momentum, JFE 142, Table B3 Panel B
evidence.quote: | LH | 0.56(0.87) | 0.00 | -0.04 | 0.58(0.89) | -0.98(-1.18) | 3.30*(1.76) | 0.08 | -0.06 | 0.03(0.06) | -0.01 | -0.06 |  [columns: | | βONFH | R2(%) | R2OOS(%) | βTONFH | βM | βSLH | R2(%) | R2OOS(%) | βROD | R2(%) | R2OOS(%) |; caption: 'Panel B: Newey and West (1986) robust t-statistics in parentheses. Samples range from April 1981 to May 2020. ... Adjusted R2, R2OOS, and slope coefficients are multiplied by 100.'; Table A1: '| Lean hogs futures | LH | 1981-04-03 | 2020-05-01 | 9499 | 08:30-13:05 | Softs |']
evidence.quote_location: on-disk copy lines 3673-3684 (caption), 3759-3784 (Table B3 cont., LH row), 3309 (sample row)

evidence.effect: Second-to-last half hour -> last half hour (SLH -> LH), lean hogs alone
evidence.rule: r_LH on r_SLH (12:05-12:35 CT return), joint regression with r_ONFH and r_M
evidence.conversion: slope 3.30 (x100) = 0.033: a 1% r_SLH predicts 3.3 bp = 1.06 ticks; typical half-hour moves are far below 1%. HE tick 0.025 c/lb x 40,000 lb = $10; at the 80 c/lb price level the source itself uses (He 2022, p.16: 'a lean hog contract with a unit price of 80 cents/pound'), 1 tick = 0.025/80 = 3.125 bp
evidence.decay_evidence: In-sample t 1.76 (10% level only); the joint model's R2_OOS is -0.06% (no OOS value)
evidence.source: Baltussen et al. (2021), Table B3 Panel B, LH row

evidence.effect: Next-day direction after a locked-limit day (limit-induced under-reaction), lean hogs
evidence.rule: logit of 1[settle(d) > settle(d-1)] on SignedLimit(d-1) (+1 locked limit-up, -1 locked limit-down, 0 else) with controls
evidence.hold: settlement to settlement (includes the overnight gap)
evidence.conversion: direction only; no return size reported. exp(1.006) = 2.73 odds ratio
evidence.sample: CME lean hogs, first five nearby contracts, 2014-2019, daily (7,264 obs.); 172 locked-limit events (39 in the first nearby)
evidence.decay_evidence: none (single 2014-2019 sample; limit days cluster in 2014)
evidence.source: He, X. (2022), Essays on extreme events in agricultural futures markets, PhD dissertation, University of Illinois, Appendix B.4, Table B.5 (working version of He and Serra, AJAE 104(5) 2022, 1724-1746)
evidence.quote: SignedLimit d−1,c 1.006*** 0.181 [Lean Hog estimate, std. error]; Obs 7,264 ... 'The exponential of the coefficient β1 is around 2.7, suggesting that on average the price is 1.7 times more likely to move in the same direction following a locked-limit day than following a non-limit day.'
evidence.quote_location: dissertation printed pp.179-180 (text lines 7665-7727) and p.200 Table B.5 (lines 8326-8346)

evidence.effect: Price path after limit moves: locked-limit days gap beyond the limit next day and stay; temporary-limit days reverse
evidence.rule: median distance to the limit in 5-minute bins, pre- and post-limit windows; post-limit window for locked days starts at the next day's open
evidence.hold: next-day open to +1 hour (locked); same-day after the touch (temporary)
evidence.conversion: locked: next-day level 0.3-0.4 c/lb beyond the old limit = 12-16 ticks = $120-160, reached at the OPEN (overnight gap, not capturable by an entry at t1 = 09:00); post-open drift not sized (figure only: 'remains persistently far'). temporary: about 0.5 c/lb (20 ticks) inside the range, but the class 'temporary' is defined by the close (hindsight), so no causal rule. Pooled lean hog and live cattle in the text. HE tick 0.025 c/lb x 40,000 lb = $10; at the 80 c/lb price level the source itself uses (He 2022, p.16: 'a lean hog contract with a unit price of 80 cents/pound'), 1 tick = 0.025/80 = 3.125 bp
evidence.sample: CME lean hogs and live cattle, first five nearby, 2014-2019, intraday
evidence.source: He (2022) dissertation, ch.3 section on Figure 3.1
evidence.quote: On the next trading day following a locked-limit day, the price jumps to a new level that is 0.3 to 0.4 cents/lb. outside the previous day's limit. The price level remains persistently far from the previous limit after one hour of trading, suggesting that price limits impede price discovery and induce market under-reaction on locked-limit days. ... In contrast, temporary-limit moves are followed by a price reversal resulting in a post-limit price level around 0.5 cents/lb. inside the trading range
evidence.quote_location: printed p.69 (text lines 3209-3230); Figure 3.1 note p.84

evidence.effect: Flash events (large intraday moves) in lean hogs: no reversal documented; moves read as fundamental
evidence.rule: events: price change of at least 2.4 c/lb within an hour (at 80 c/lb), USDA-report days excluded
evidence.sample: CME lean hogs and corn, 2014-2019, limit order book, 1,253 non-announcement days
evidence.source: He (2022) dissertation ch.2 (= He, Serra, Garcia, AJAE 103(2) 2021, 743-764, 'Resilience in Flash Events in the Corn and Lean Hog Futures Markets')
evidence.quote: the revised threshold requires the price to change by at least 2.4 cents/pound ($960 per contract) within an hour. ... The temporal duration of the events (around 50 minutes in both markets) corresponds closely to the recent findings which show that it takes about an hour for low latency agricultural markets to absorb fully fundamental information from USDA releases

evidence.effect: Hog report window: NASS Quarterly Hogs and Pigs release time (after HE's 13:05 CT close, except noon-ET releases)
evidence.rule: release normally 15:00 ET (14:00 CT, after the close; reaction is overnight, out of scope); a Friday noon-ET release (11:00 CT) falls inside the session
evidence.quote: has rescheduled release of the December Cattle on Feed and Hogs and Pigs reports to Thursday, Dec. 20 at 3:00 pm ET. They were previously scheduled for release on Friday, Dec. 21 at Noon ET.

evidence.effect: Hog report window: USDA LMR swine report statutory deadlines inside the HE session
evidence.rule: prior-day purchased report by 08:00 CT; prior-day slaughtered by 10:00 CT; morning report by 11:00 CT; afternoon report by 15:00 CT (after close). Deadlines, not fixed instants
evidence.conversion: no published intraday futures response found (searched); unknown, not rejected
evidence.quote: The Secretary shall publish the information obtained under this paragraph in the morning report as soon as practicable, but not later than 11:00 a.m. Central Time, on each reporting day. ... (I) in the case of information regarding barrows and gilts purchased or priced, not later than 8:00 a.m. Central Time, and (II) in the case of information regarding barrows and gilts slaughtered, not later than 10:00 a.m. Central Time ... in the afternoon report as soon as practicable, but not later than 3:00 p.m. Central Time

evidence.effect: Limit events lead to persistent price changes (commodity futures, multi-market)
evidence.source: Janardanan, Qiao, Rouwenhorst (2019), On commodity price limits, J. Futures Markets 39 (class-level; LE reader's)
evidence.quote: We find little evidence that limits events are the result of speculative activity, but instead associated with shocks to fundamentals that lead to persistent price changes. [abstract via OpenAlex metadata only]
